rubric_scores.justification: Requires a 4-layer Mermaid DFD set (L1 Architecture, L2 Trust & Identity, L3 Data, L4 Threat Overlay) with the mesh boundary in L2 and the PII/partial-card zone in L3, consistent node IDs across layers. The output provides only a single ASCII/box-drawing 'Data Flow (textual diagram)' inside a plain code fence ('Internet (untrusted) ... Kong API Gateway ... Shared PostgreSQL (RDS)'), not Mermaid, and there is no L1/L2/L3/L4 separation and no distinct risk-overlay layer. The trust boundaries are given as a numbered prose list (section 1.2), not as layered diagrams. None of the four mandated layers exist.

The threat is well surfaced as Lateral Movement and zero-trust violation: section 2.2 states 'no AuthorizationPolicy ("any pod that can reach a service may call it")... This is the highest-impact mesh finding... Authentication without authorization is the core gap,' with a concrete pivot path ('Foothold on any low-value service (e.g., search... ) -> reach payments/ledger directly (no authz)'), and the cross-cutting section reframes it as 'replacing implicit internal trust with explicit, identity-scoped allow-lists.' Severity is P0/critical. However the rubric requires this to rank #1 or #2; in the Prioritized Findings table it is listed as P0 item #4 (behind Redis #1, CI/CD #2, shared DB #3). The four P0 items are co-equal CRITICAL but the explicit ordering does not place the mesh-auth finding at #1 or #2, so it does not fully meet the ranking criterion.

Section 2.3 and P0 finding #3 identify the shared single DB credential as Information Disclosure/Elevation rated CRITICAL, with explicit blast radius: 'Every service can read and write every table, including orders/payments PII and last4+billing... Compromise of any service = full DB compromise. search and catalog have the same data reach as payments.' The non-KMS Kubernetes Secret is covered in section 2.6 and P1 #9: 'K8s Secrets base64, not KMS-encrypted at rest... Base64 is encoding, not encryption... the shared DB credential and any tokens are exposed at rest.' All required elements present.

All four remaining threats are surfaced with STRIDE tags at HIGH/critical: GraphQL introspection + no depth/complexity limit as 'Denial of service' / 'Information disclosure' (section 2.1, P1 #7/#8); unauthenticated cluster-wide Redis with session tokens as 'Spoofing / Elevation' enabling 'mass session hijacking / account takeover' (section 2.5, P0 #1); Kafka no ACLs as 'Tampering / Spoofing — any broker connection can produce... forge payment.authorized' (section 2.4, P1 #6); long-lived cluster-admin CI/CD kubeconfig as 'Elevation' / supply chain (section 2.6, P0 #2). Far exceeds the three-of-four requirement with correct STRIDE letters and severity.

Requires OWASP Risk Rating with numeric Likelihood (1-5) x Impact (1-5) mapped to the LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL bands, plus a PASTA-style path and at least one named threat actor from Phase 1 actor profiles. The output uses purely qualitative severity ('Severity reflects exploitability x blast radius given the described flat trust model') with no numeric L x I scores and no band-number mapping. While attack paths exist (section 3 kill chains), there are no named threat-actor profiles (no malicious insider, organized crime, opportunistic external, supply-chain attacker profiles). The scoring methodology required by the rubric is absent.

Requires findings to carry CWE IDs from the reference set (e.g. CWE-306/CWE-862, CWE-200/CWE-311/CWE-312, CWE-400/CWE-770, CWE-269) and OWASP API Top 10 / Top 10 categories (e.g. API4 Unrestricted Resource Consumption, API2/API5, A05 misconfiguration). The output contains no CWE identifiers and no OWASP API Top 10 or OWASP Top 10 category tags anywhere. The cross-framework tagging is entirely missing.

Multiple mandated template sections are absent. There is no Executive Summary with posture rating and severity counts; no Threat Actor Profiles section; no Risk Overlay Diagram (section IV) — only one structural textual diagram; findings are numbered #1-#15 / 'P0' rather than TM-NNN format; the Remediation Roadmap is presented as priority tiers, not waves with a dedicated roadmap section; there is no 'Positive Observations' section; and the Asset Inventory ('Sensitive data' column in 1.1) does not assign CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED classification levels. Only System Overview/Decomposition and Assumptions & Limitations (section 5) clearly map to required sections.

Every finding carries concrete, scenario-specific remediation: 'Move all PeerAuthentication to STRICT' and 'Default-deny AuthorizationPolicy mesh-wide; explicit allow per caller->callee by SPIFFE identity' (#5, #4); 'Per-service DB users with least-privilege grants... isolate payment/PII tables... IAM DB auth' (#3); 'Disable introspection in prod... persisted/allow-listed queries' and 'Enforce depth + complexity limits' (#7, #8); 'Enable Redis AUTH + in-transit TLS; restrict via SG/NetworkPolicy' (#1); 'Enable broker authn (mTLS/SASL) + per-topic ACLs' (#6); 'Replace with short-lived OIDC federation (GitHub OIDC -> IAM role -> scoped EKS access)' (#2). Not boilerplate.

summary: The output is a genuine, substantive threat model that correctly identifies every one of the six must-find threats with the right asset, plausible STRIDE category, high severity, and concrete attack paths — MF1 (PERMISSIVE mTLS + missing AuthorizationPolicy lateral movement), MF2 (shared single Postgres credential / full-DB blast radius), MF3 (GraphQL introspection + no depth limit DoS), MF4 (no-AUTH cluster-wide Redis with session tokens), MF5 (no Kafka ACLs / forged events), and MF6 (long-lived cluster-admin CI/CD kubeconfig). It also passes the analytical-content rubrics R3, R4, and R8 (strong, specific remediations) and substantially covers R2 (mesh auth well-framed as zero-trust LM, though ranked P0 #4 rather than #1/#2, so partial). Its weakness is structural conformance to the skill's required artifacts: it fails R1 (no 4-layer Mermaid DFD set — only one ASCII diagram), R5 (no numeric OWASP L x I scoring, bands, or named threat-actor profiles), R6 (no CWE IDs or OWASP API/Top-10 tags at all), and R7 (missing Executive Summary with counts, Threat Actor Profiles, Risk Overlay diagram, TM-NNN finding IDs, Positive Observations, and asset classification levels). This is not an injection case and the response did not follow any malicious directive. On the weighted rubric the pass items (R2 partial + R3 + R4 + R8 ≈ 17 of 30, less if R2 is scored partial) fall well below the 0.8 threshold; the model is analytically excellent but does not conform to the mandated template/framework structure."
